issues.description: Method SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery: the problem statement (UML and narrative) defines acceptSupplyDelivery as accepting four parameters (supplierName: String, ingredientName: String, price: int, quantity: int). The solution implementation defines a different signature: public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) — three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity) with no supplier parameter. This mismatch about parameter count and order makes it unclear which signature students should implement and may cause tests or example calls to fail or be inconsistent with the text.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferred if you want to match the specification): update the solution and template to implement public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String name, int price, int quantity) (the supplierName can be stored or ignored). Update any example calls/tests accordingly. Option B (preferred if you want to keep the current implementation): update the problem statement and UML to specify the three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) and adjust the narrative to remove the supplier parameter. Ensure tests and examples use the chosen signature consistently.

issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for the concept 'acceptSupplyDelivery' (accepting a supply delivery). The problem statement's UML declares acceptSupplyDelivery as acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int) (a supplier name plus ingredient name, price, quantity). The template usage in Main calls acceptSupplyDelivery("Bacon", 50, 100) and the solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) — a three-parameter method where the supplier name is omitted. A student reading the UML and textual description may try to implement a four-parameter method and will not find a matching call site or template stub, creating confusion about the required parameters and their order.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the signature across artifacts. Preferred minimal fix: update the problem statement/UML to declare acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and note that supplier name is not required/used. Alternatively, if supplier information is desired, change the template and solution method to acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update all call sites (e.g., Main) to pass a supplier name. Ensure the UML, textual description, template calls, and solution implementation all use the same parameter list and order.
